newsitem.title: USA: Moody's warns NYS might rely more on one-shots.
newsitem.headline: Moody's warns NYS might rely more on one-shots.

text.p: New York State's proposed budget for fiscal 1998 "is represented" as only including $66 million of one-shots but relies on a big cash surplus and the final pact might contain more, a rating agency said Monday.

Moody's Investors Service noted that the fiscal 1997 surplus of $943 million is fully included in the fiscal 1998 budget proposed by the Pataki Administration, which leaves a gap to be filled in fiscal 1999.

"In addition, experience has show that the final adopted budget is likely to make greater use of nonrecurring revenues to achieve budget balance than the proposed budget, which could have the effect of increasing projected out-year budget gaps," said Bob Kurtter, a Moody's analyst, in prepared remarks.

Total spending for capital projects declines slightly from the 1997 fiscal year, as does the pay-as-you-go share of financing, which slips to 24 percent from 26 percent in fiscal 1998, and is expected to drop to 14 percent in 2002. Yet Authority borrowing rises from 35 percent to 51 percent of capital plan financing with federal funds accounting for 28 percent to 32 percent.
General obligation bonds represent 13 percent of the capital plan, but fall to only three percent in fiscal 2002. Over 57 percent of the capital plan goes to transportation projects.
